title: 2023 AMC 12B Problem 24
statement:
Suppose that \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) are positive integers satisfying all of the following relations.

\[ \begin{aligned} abcd &= 2^6\cdot 3^9\cdot 5^7\\ \operatorname{lcm}(a,b) &= 2^3\cdot 3^2\cdot 5^3\\ \operatorname{lcm}(a,c) &= 2^3\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^3\\ \operatorname{lcm}(a,d) &= 2^3\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^3\\ \operatorname{lcm}(b,c) &= 2^1\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\\ \operatorname{lcm}(b,d) &= 2^2\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\\ \operatorname{lcm}(c,d) &= 2^2\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2 \end{aligned} \]

What is \(\gcd(a,b,c,d)?\)

solutions.text:
Handle each prime separately using the exponents of \(a,b,c,d.\)

Prime \(2\) (total \(6\)): \(\max(b,c)=1\) forces \(a=3;\) then \(b+c+d=3\) with \(\max(b,d)=\max(c,d)=2\) gives \(d=2\) and \(\{b,c\}=\{0,1\},\) so the minimum exponent is \(0.\)

Prime \(3\) (total \(9\)): \(\max(a,b)=2\) with the other lcms equal to \(3\) forces \(c=d=3;\) then \(a+b=3\) with \(\max(a,b)=2\) gives \(\{a,b\}=\{1,2\},\) so the minimum is \(1.\)

Prime \(5\) (total \(7\)): \(\max(a,b)=3\) with \(\max(b,c),\) \(\max(b,d),\max(c,d)=2\) forces \(a=3;\) then \(b+c+d=4\) with each \(\le 2\) and pairwise maxima \(2\) gives two of them equal to \(2\) and one equal to \(0,\) so the minimum is \(0.\)

Therefore \(\gcd(a,b,c,d)=2^0\cdot 3^1\cdot 5^0=3.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Work one prime at a time; \(\gcd\) uses the minimum exponent and \(\operatorname{lcm}\) the maximum
For each prime, pin down the four exponents from the max (lcm) and total (product) conditions, then take the minimum
